open_obligations.what_is_open: Construction and proof of one fully observable confidence interval with uniform coverage over null, local, smoothness-critical, and regular regimes, together with the stated regime-adaptive half-widths.
open_obligations.obstruction: The population Gaussianization theorem does not establish observable common-multiplier quantile consistency or anti-concentration through variance degeneracy, and the available pilot-Hessian and covariance controls do not supply that missing uniform coupling.
open_obligations.attempted: A population Gaussian--quadratic interval for \(d\ge1\) and an exact Brownian-bridge quadratic interval at the \(d=0\) uniform null were derived, but neither construction is fully observable and uniformly valid across the requested mixed regimes.
open_obligations.partial_result: For \(d\ge1\), the infeasible population interval centered at \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}\), with half-width equal to the population Gaussian--quadratic absolute quantile divided by \(n\), a vanishing bounded--Lipschitz smoothing allowance, and a Markov allowance for the corrected remainder, has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\). At \((J_y^*,J_z^*)\) its half-width is of order \[\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-2s_z/(2s_z+d)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{d/(2s_z+d)}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2.\] For \(d=0\) at the uniform null, the interval \[\left[\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}-q^0_{1-\alpha}/n,\;\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}+q^0_{1-\alpha}/n\right]\] has coverage converging to \(1-\alpha\), where \(q^0_{1-\alpha}\) is the lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt\). Neither interval resolves the requested fully observable, uniformly mixed-regime calibration.

prose_updates.tldr: For \(d\ge1\), conditional squared Wasserstein distance has an anisotropic boundary geometry: inverse ellipticity smooths outcome frequencies while covariate resolution replicates the ordered spectrum. The sign-paired family supplies the zero and quadratic lower components, while a separate fixed-frequency, constant-in-\(z\) two-point family supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) component; together they yield the intrinsic lower frontier \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\), while the zero estimator, the explicit Gram-corrected estimator, median SmoothCOT, and, when available, median direct-COT give a computable observable upper envelope; the nontrivial quadratic zone remains an honest unmatched bracket. Under the theorem's stated triangular conditions, the infeasible oracle-score, population-kernel statistic has Gaussian limits for \(d\ge1\); no observable-experiment Gaussianization or calibration is claimed. The separate \(d=0\) branch recovers the two-sample del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet law and \(n^{-1}\) scale. Uniform mixed-regime calibration remains open.
